**Date:** 22 Jul 2026

**Issue:** The microcontroller execution was permanently trapped, preventing the main loop from acquiring live MPU6050 and INA219 sensor data for the TinyML based conditional monitor framework.

**Issue Location:** Firmware / X-CUBE-AI auto-generated validation template (app_x-cube-ai.c or equivalent AI wrapper).

**Diagnosis method:**
- Used the STM32CubeIDE debugger to pause execution during the freeze.
- Inspected the Call Stack and stepped through the AI initialization and execution functions.
- Observed that the CPU was indefinitely stuck inside a do { ... } while(); loop generated by X-CUBE-AI, preventing execution from ever returning to the main while(1) loop in main.c.

**Mitigation 1:** Commented out the do { ... } while() loop construct within the X-CUBE-AI generated code, effectively converting the AI execution block from an infinite loop into a single-shot function.
- Outcome: The bug resolved. The AI model performed inference on the live data buffer and successfully returned control to the main program loop, enabling continuous, real-time predictive maintenance monitoring.

**Hypothetical Root cause:** When generating X-CUBE-AI project code, STMicroelectronics often includes a default validation template designed to test the neural network's performance continuously using static dummy data. This template relies on a blocking do-while loop that intentionally hijacks the CPU. In a real-world TinyML application, this validation architecture traps the execution flow, starving the hardware peripherals (I2C, sensors) of CPU time.

**Learning:** HAL generated XcubeAI code is often structured for isolated software validation rather than real-world hardware integration. For a real-time conditional monitor framework, the X-CUBE-AI inference function must be explicitly modified by stripping out validation loops so it acts as a single-shot, non-blocking call. This ensures the master while(1) loop retains absolute control over data acquisition and telemetry pipelines.
